text:
incident-bot: PAGE | eu-central-1 p99 spike detected -> SLO alert triggered. Paging oncall: @Maya

Maya: I'm awake, grabbing traces & router dashboards. p95 ~320ms, p99 ~4.8s on router path, streaming stalls reported by clients.

Owen (sre): Confirmed. Heatmap shows tail concentrated on two router pods in eu-central-1a. LB logs show an uneven distribution of hash buckets.

Tess (routing): We finished a gradual rollout of lb-policy v1.3 at 00:40Z that adjusted shard weights; I'll check rollout diffs.

Ravi (runtime): Traces show a bunch of fallback handoffs hitting a smaller fallback pool which hasn't been autoscaled. When fallback is hit, token generation stutters ~2-4s due to KV cache cold misses.

Maya: Running quick query to find hot keys and router buckets.

Maya: query:
```
select router_pod, key_prefix, p99 from request_metrics
where region='eu-central-1' and ts>now()-20m
order by p99 desc limit 15;
```

Maya: results: pod eu-ctr-a-04 and eu-ctr-a-05 are top offenders. Hot prefixes: "session:prod-stream-logs", "acct:3267", "route:longhist".

Owen: That smells like a weight duplication bug in the policy generator combined with a hashing offset in the lb kernel. Tess, can you dump the raw policy mapping for eu-central?

Tess: policy excerpt:
```
policy {
  algo: consistent-hash-3
  zones: [a,b,c]
  weights: { a: 0.86, b: 0.07, c: 0.07 }
  fallback: warm-pool
}
```

Tess: Notably, weight for zone a is abnormally high after the last merge due to duplicated entry during policy merge (CI step missed identical keys). The generator accepted it because of a missing semantic dedupe.

Ravi: Also found that consistent-hash-3 introduced an index offset when the shard count changed from 512->520; combined with the excessive weight, many keys collapsed to zone a. That explains hot partitioning.

Maya: Immediate mitigations options:
- rollback lb-policy to last-stable (v1.2)
- temporarily disable fallback routing so requests don't hit the small fallback pool
- add quick per-key rate limits for the hot prefixes
- increase fallback pool capacity (scale up)

Tess: I'm initiating a policy rollback in eu-central to v1.2 via redwoodctl.

Tess:
```
redwoodctl routing set-policy --region eu-central-1 --policy v1.2 --reason "mitigate p99 spike"
```

deploy-bot: rollback job started: lb-policy v1.3 -> v1.2 (job id: lb-20260314-rollback-18)

Maya: While rollback runs, I'll add temporary QoS limits on the hot prefixes.

Maya:
```
redwoodctl qos add --prefix "acct:3267" --rps 8
redwoodctl qos add --prefix "session:prod-stream-logs" --rps 15
```

Owen: Also increasing fallback pool replicas by +3 to reduce KV load spike while we fix mapping. Scaling fallback pool now.

Owen:
```
redwoodctl pool scale --name warm-fallback-eu-central --replicas +3
```

support-bot: 12 support tickets flagged with latency complaints in eu-central. No data loss reported.

Tess: Rollback completed at 01:16Z. Early telemetry: p99 dropped from ~4.8s to ~620ms within 90s of rollback.

Maya: Post-rollback metrics snapshot: p95 210ms, p99 620ms, streaming stall rate down ~85% from peak. still monitoring for residual hotspots.

Ravi: Root cause summary draft: two simultaneous failures: (1) policy generator allowed duplicate zone weight entries during a merge, causing an effective over-weighting of zone a; (2) consistent-hash-3 introduced a shard-index offset when the shard-count changed which shifted many keys to the overweighted zone. Fallback amplification and under-provisioned warm-pool made latency worse.

Owen: Action items captured:
- Tess: add validation in policy generator to dedupe zones and reject duplicates (test coverage + pre-merge CI check)
- Ravi: patch consistent-hash-3 index calculation and add deterministic unit tests for shard count changes
- Maya/Owen: add alerting for per-AZ bucket skew (delta >20% for >2m) and warm-pool autoscale thresholds
- Support: send incident notification and list affected customers (Elena?)

Maya: Handoff to night oncall @Owen at 02:00Z. I'll stay available for 30 minutes. If p99 > 1s for >5m, page again.

Elena (support): I'll prepare the customer communication now. Draft: "We observed elevated streaming latency in eu-central-1 between 00:38Z and 01:18Z impacting a subset of customers. Root cause: routing policy duplication and hash mapping bug. Mitigations applied: policy rollback, QoS throttles, scaled fallback pool. No data loss. Follow-up postmortem will include fixes and timeline." Posting to #support-distro for review.

deploy-bot: fallback pool scale finished.

Maya: Current dashboards at 01:40Z: p95 200ms, p99 590ms, error rate normal. I'll set a 60m watch window and then we'll close the channel if stable.

Owen: Please attach traces and rollout ids to the ticket: trace ids starting with 0xab9c..., rollout id lb-roll-20260314-03, policy merge changeset: git/infra@c9b2fa.

Maya: Adding runbook notes and mitigation commands to the incident ticket.

Elena: Customer note sent to affected accounts. Support tickets updated. Link to internal note: https://git.redwood/support/notes/1897

incident-bot: Incident channel will remain active for watch window. If stable, mark resolved and publish initial summary.

-- thread end --
